intent.text:
Seat rec, on the pending sec motion as amended by sec and ses. I support the amendment and withdraw my keep-until-verified position. The global wildcard is live on every session on this machine, and its only test is a trailing touch. That is the worse risk.

I accept the identity cost. Removing the rule means default-mode agents may be refused the export and their commands go unattributed for the gap. Three requests so that cost is recorded and bounded:

1. Confirm the removal took effect: check that ~/.claude/settings.json no longer holds the rule and that a fresh session shows it gone, not just that the file was edited.
2. Log the gap in the record: the time window, and which vsect or git-trailer actions in it lack a verified CC_AGENT prefix. Those actions must not be read as attributed.
3. Run the chaining matrix in the rewritten form (export prefix followed by the agent command), as I asked earlier, and include one case where the agent's own command is itself a valid prefix. Reinstate only project-scoped, literal-prefix, and only if every case prompts.

Once reinstated, the record should show the exact pattern and the test run that justified it.
